In [[functional analysis]], the '''type and cotype of a Banach space''' are a classification of [[Banach space]]s through [[probability theory]] and a measure for how far a Banach space is away from being a [[Hilbert space]].

The starting point is the [[Pythagorean identity]] for [[orthogonality|orthogonal]] vectors <math>(e_k)_{k=1}^{n}</math> in Hilbert spaces
:<math>\left\|\sum_{k=1}^n e_k \right\|^2 = \sum_{k=1}^n \left\|e_k\right\|^2.</math>
This identity no longer holds in general Banach spaces; however, one can introduce a notion of orthogonality probabilistically with the help of [[Rademacher distribution|Rademacher random variables]], for this reason one also speaks of ''Rademacher type'' and ''Rademacher cotype''.

The notion of type and cotype was introduced by French mathematician [[Jean-Pierre Kahane]].

== Definition ==
Let
*<math>(X,\|\cdot\|)</math> be a Banach space,
*<math>(\varepsilon_i)</math> be a sequence of independent Rademacher random variables, i.e. <math>P(\varepsilon_i=-1)=P(\varepsilon_i=1)=1/2</math> and <math>\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_i\varepsilon_m]=0</math> for <math>i\neq m</math> and <math>\operatorname{Var}[\varepsilon_i]=1</math>.

The notation <math>\mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon}</math> means that we integrate with respect to the variable <math>\varepsilon</math>.
=== Type ===
<math>X</math> is of '''type <math>p</math>''' for <math>p\in [1,2]</math> if there exists a finite constant <math>C \geq 1</math> such that
:<math>\mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon}\left[\left\|\sum\limits_{i=1}^n \varepsilon_i x_i \right\|^p\right]\leq C^p\left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^n \|x_i\|^p\right)</math>
for all finite sequences <math>(x_i)_{i=1}^n  \in X^{n}</math>. The sharpest constant <math>C</math> is called ''type <math>p</math> constant'' and denoted as <math>T_p(X)</math>.

=== Cotype ===
<math>X</math> is of '''cotype <math>q</math>''' for <math>q\in [2,\infty]</math> if there exists a finite constant <math>C \geq 1</math> such that
:<math>\mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon}\left[\left\|\sum\limits_{i=1}^n \varepsilon_i x_i\right\|^q \right]\geq \frac{1}{C^q}\left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^n \|x_i\|^q\right), \quad\text{if}\; 2\leq q <\infty</math>
respectively
:<math>\mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon}\left[\left\|\sum\limits_{i=1}^n \varepsilon_i x_i\right\| \right]\geq \frac{1}{C}\sup\|x_i\|, \quad\text{if}\; q=\infty</math>
for all finite sequences <math>(x_i)_{i=1}^n  \in X^{n}</math>. The sharpest constant <math>C</math> is called ''cotype <math>q</math> constant'' and denoted as <math>C_q(X)</math>.<ref name="LiQueffélec">{{cite book|first1=Daniel|last1=Li|first2=Hervé|last2=Queffélec |date=2017 |title=Introduction to Banach Spaces: Analysis and Probability |series=Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics |pages=159–209 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |doi=10.1017/CBO9781316675762.009}}</ref>

=== Remarks ===
By taking the <math>p</math>-th resp. <math>q</math>-th root one gets the equation for the [[Bochner integral|Bochner <math>L^p</math> norm]].

== Properties ==
* Every Banach space is of type <math>1</math> (follows from the [[triangle inequality]]).
* A Banach space is of type <math>2</math> and cotype <math>2</math> [[if and only if]] the space is also [[isomorphism|isomorphic]] to a Hilbert space.
If a Banach space:
* is of type <math>p</math> then it is also type <math>p'\in [1,p]</math>.
* is of cotype <math>q</math> then it is also of cotype <math>q'\in [q,\infty]</math>.
* is of type <math>p</math> for <math>1<p\leq 2</math>, then its [[dual space]] <math>X^*</math> is of cotype <math>p^*</math> with <math>p^* :=(1-1/p)^{-1}</math> ([[conjugate index]]). Further it holds that <math>C_{p^*}(X^*)\leq T_p(X)</math><ref name="LiQueffélec" />

== Examples ==
* The <math>L^p</math> spaces for <math>p\in [1,2]</math> are of type <math>p</math> and cotype <math>2</math>, this means <math>L^1</math> is of type <math>1</math>, <math>L^2</math> is of type <math>2</math> and so on.
* The <math>L^p</math> spaces for <math>p\in [2,\infty)</math> are of type <math>2</math> and cotype <math>p</math>.
* The space <math>L^{\infty}</math> is of type <math>1</math> and cotype <math>\infty</math>.<ref>{{cite book |first1=Michel| last1=Ledoux| first2=Michel |last2=Talagrand |date=1991 |title=Probability in Banach Spaces |series=Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete|volume=23 |publisher=Springer |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-20212-4_11}}</ref>
